issues.title: "Dev-only" flag guard is documented everywhere but not implemented
issues.description: The file header, plan, seam doc, and CLAUDE.md all state the flag is "DEFAULT OFF and DEV-ONLY", and the plan's failure-mode table cites "flag is default-off + dev-only" as the structural guard against silently discarding a user's localStorage workspace (flag-ON starts from an empty corpus; no migration until S4). But `isCorpusEnabled()` contains no `NODE_ENV`/dev check — `localStorage.setItem("corpus-fs-enabled", "1")` in any production deployment, or `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS=1` in a production build, enables the corpus path and makes the user's existing workspace vanish from view. The promised data-loss guard is absent.

issues.title: With corpus flag ON, `onRehydrateStorage` can clobber rehydrated corpus state with stale v2 localStorage data
issues.description: The migration check reads `localStorage` keys (`workspace-v2`, `workspace-zustand-v1`) regardless of which storage backend is active. When the flag is ON and a legacy `workspace-v2` key exists but `workspace-zustand-v1` doesn't, `migrateFromV2()` runs on every load, overwriting the just-rehydrated OPFS-backed state with old v2 data (which is then persisted back to the corpus) — both corrupting flag-ON state and contradicting the documented "flag-ON starts from an empty corpus, no migration in S1" contract.

issues.title: Corpus-backed `setItem` has no write serialization or debounce → stale-write race and write amplification
issues.description: The localStorage path debounces writes by 300 ms, but `createCorpusBackedStorage` issues an OPFS `writeFile` for every store `set()` with no queueing: overlapping writes to `state/<name>.json` each open their own `createWritable()` staging file, and whichever `close()` lands last wins — an earlier (stale) snapshot can complete after a newer one, persisting regressed state. It also turns every keystroke into a full-blob OPFS write chain.

issues.title: Fail-loud parse contract is undermined by silent per-entry drops
issues.description: The header mandates that a malformed manifest "never" parse into something that masks data loss, yet `sources.filter(isObject)`, `artifacts.filter(isObject)`, and `customTypeIds.filter(typeof === "string")` silently discard corrupted entries (and `createdAt`/`updatedAt` are silently replaced with `new Date()`), so a partially corrupted manifest parses "successfully" with sources/artifact pointers missing — precisely the masquerade the contract (and test G11) is supposed to prevent, in the module S4 will trust as its index.

issues.title: `workspaceSlug` collisions map distinct workspace titles to the same directory
issues.description: Lowercasing plus collapsing all non-`[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` runs means titles like "My Workspace", "my workspace!", and "MY-WORKSPACE" all slug to `my-workspace`, so two different workspaces would share one `workspaces/<slug>/` tree and silently overwrite each other's manifest and artifacts once S4 wires the layout in. The module is explicitly the S1-frozen contract S2–S4 bind to, so the collision semantics deserve resolution (or a documented uniquing scheme) now.

issues.title: Path builders throw plain `Error`, not `CorpusError`, breaking the module's typed-error model
issues.description: `workspaceSlug`/`safeSegment`/`artifactVersionPath` throw bare `Error`s (e.g. for an all-unicode title such as "日本語"), while the corpus module's stated contract is that failures reify as `CorpusError` with a discriminated kind — callers switching exhaustively on `CorpusErrorKind` will miss these, and an entirely-CJK workspace title becomes an unclassified crash path in S4.

issues.title: `manifestVersion` is validated as a number but never checked against `MANIFEST_VERSION`
issues.description: A future v2 manifest (or garbage like `manifestVersion: 999`) parses as if current with unknown fields silently dropped, defeating the point of carrying a version field in a fail-loud codec; an explicit version gate would turn forward-incompatibility into a typed error.

issues.title: Comment claims a fresh ArrayBuffer view is passed, but the code passes the caller's array directly
issues.description: The comment "Pass a fresh ArrayBuffer view; some implementations dislike shared buffers" describes a copy that isn't made — `w.write(bytes)` forwards the original `Uint8Array`. Either make the copy the comment promises or delete the comment; as written it documents behavior that doesn't exist.

issues.title: Fake's `readFile` returns the live stored array, unlike real OPFS
issues.description: `writeFile` defensively copies but `readFile` hands back the stored `Uint8Array` by reference, so a consumer that mutates a read buffer would corrupt the fake's state while real OPFS (which materializes fresh bytes from `arrayBuffer()`) would be unaffected. Since fake-vs-OPFS divergence is the plan's own top residual risk and the contract suite is the substitutability proof, the fake should return `bytes.slice()`.

issues.title: `docs/user_research/property-tests.json` untracked but not ignored
issues.description: Commit 2dc403e removed the file from tracking ("swept in by git add -A; restore to untracked") but added no ignore entry, so the next `git add -A` will sweep it right back in; add it (or its directory pattern) to .gitignore to make the untracking stick.
